title: Everything in AutoSecOps
sub: What AutoSecOps does from the first alert to the audit record, grouped the way your team works.

items: Every alert triaged around the clock: SIEM, EDR, email, identity, cloud
Duplicates removed, indicators of compromise (IOCs) extracted
Enrichment from threat intelligence and your own lookup tables
AI verdict, severity and summary; case opened in the same run
Read-only lookups and enrichment run without waiting
Disabling accounts or isolating devices waits for a person
See each action’s arguments, then approve, edit or reject
One approval inbox, plus approval buttons in Slack threads
Recommendation-only mode before automation is switched on
Agents can call only the tools you allow
Isolated sandbox with no internet access by default
Instructions hidden in an alert cannot take over the agent
Token budgets per agent; AI keys stay outside the sandbox
Workspace chat that works across tables, cases and workflows
Skill packs: triage, hunting, detection rules, AWS access, incident response, threat intel
Drag-and-drop builder, or describe the playbook in chat
Triggers: webhooks, schedules, case events, forms, manual runs and API
Conditions, loops, parallel branches, retries and sub-workflows
Runs survive restarts; step-by-step history, rerun from any step
Checks before publishing; locked versions with one-step rollback
Tables for allowlists, assets and IOCs; forms that start workflows
Also automates IT, finance, revenue operations, people, legal and engineering work
Built-in cases with status, priority, severity, tags and custom fields
Tasks, sub-cases, SLA tracking and required fields at closing
Comments, attachments, activity feed and full version history
One-click workflows from a case, inputs filled from case data
Case copilot: AI chat on every case; mention the agent in comments
Proposing agent, approver and time recorded in the case
Duration metrics, closing reasons and reports for management
2,000+ integrations: SIEM, EDR, identity, cloud, email, ticketing and chat
Catalog of Model Context Protocol (MCP) servers, one-click connect
AutoSecOps MCP server: Claude Code and Cursor manage workflows and cases
Watchtower: see what coding agents call over MCP, end sessions if needed
Your own Python actions and playbooks, synced with GitHub, GitLab or Bitbucket
Tunnels reach internal systems with scoped, short-lived access
First-party EDR, NDR and SIEM sensors if you have none
Managed cloud: we handle installation and updates
On-premises on one server in minutes, or Kubernetes via Helm
Fully air-gapped: local AI model, license checked offline
Cloud AI providers: OpenAI, Anthropic, AWS Bedrock, Azure, Google, Mistral, OpenRouter
Self-hosted AI: Singularity Foundation Models, Ollama, vLLM or LiteLLM
Setup, configuration and training by our team
Single sign-on (SAML, OIDC), SCIM user sync and IP allowlists
Custom roles, scoped permissions and service accounts
Every action in the audit log; session logs and revocation
Encrypted secrets with masking, per-environment scope and external vaults
Audit-ready records for Turkish KVKK, BDDK and Law No. 7545
Security mapped to OWASP Top 10, LLM and Agentic Top 10

specs.v: Managed cloud, on-premises (single server or Kubernetes) or fully air-gapped
2,000+ integrations across SIEM, EDR, identity, cloud, email, ticketing and chat
Singularity Foundation Models, major cloud AI providers or self-hosted models via Ollama, vLLM, LiteLLM
Single sign-on, SCIM, custom roles, IP allowlists and a full audit log
KVKK (Turkish data protection), BDDK (banking regulator) and Law No. 7545
Platform and AI stay on your network with on-premises deployment and a local model

top: Critical actions wait for your approval
gaps: Regulation: the decks sell on KVKK, BDDK and Cybersecurity Law No. 7545 (audit-ready, one-click reports) and on DORA and NIS2 deadlines. The page names none of them.
Buyer worry: can an instruction hidden in an alert steer the agent? The deck cites EchoLeak (CVE-2025-32711) and shows a poisoned alert failing. The page never mentions prompt injection.
Data claim caveat: the deck says prompts go to the AI provider if a cloud model is chosen. “Data never leaves” holds only with on-premises deployment and a local model.
Speed differentiator: the decks show weeks to minutes for connecting a tool or building a playbook, and days to ready for audit evidence. The page has no before-and-after.
